name: Low-Block 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes quickly to the forwards after a save or claim.
Support full-back stays back and helps his wide midfielder defend.

Central defender in a deep block. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: a deep block is defended by clearing the box. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: a deep block is defended by clearing the box. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Wide midfielder tracks back to help the full-back and keeps the bank of four narrow.
Defensive central midfielder protects the space in front of the defence.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the ball back in front of the box.
Wide midfielder on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds the ball up so the team can move up the pitch.
Advanced Forward runs in behind on the counter. Poacher is the alternate.

description: Two compact banks of four with two forwards retained as direct counter outlets.
whyGood: It keeps defensive jobs simple while preserving an immediate route out after regains.
whyThisShape: Two compact banks of four that defend deep and narrow, with two forwards kept as outlets. It gives the opponent no space in the middle and breaks out quickly with a runner and a hold-up forward.
whenToUse: Protecting a lead, or away against a stronger side. It suits disciplined players and wide midfielders who work hard to recover.
whenNotToUse: When you need to control the ball or score, since the team will be under pressure for long periods.

instructionRationale.Much Lower Line of Engagement: Bring the front line back into the low block; this deliberately concedes territory.
instructionRationale.Much Deeper Defensive Line: Protect the space behind the back line in a deep block; sustained pressure and shots from outside remain risks.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Lower Tempo: Allow the passing structure to form during settled possession; a selected Counter instruction still applies immediately after regains.
instructionRationale.Narrow Defensive Width: Protect the central lanes and keep defenders close enough to cover one another; outside deliveries remain a trade-off.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Less Urgent Pressing: Prioritise the block over chasing possession; the counter outlets remain available after regains.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: Centre-backs with reliable positioning and concentration
Wide midfielders willing and able to recover into the defensive bank
Central midfielders disciplined enough to protect the space in front of the box
One forward who can hold the ball up
One forward who can attack space on the counter
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
The deep block deliberately concedes territory; check chances and effective deliveries allowed rather than assuming a deeper line protects a lead.
Standard attacking width keeps wide escape outlets available. Defensive width is set separately; a compact block does not require narrow possession play.
